third_party.changes: mesh split into one node per physical control with pivots; re-based into the GoldenEye joypad model frame (GjoypadZ) and scaled to its 788-unit width; normal / metallic-roughness / emissive maps dropped; base-colour textures resized to 1024 px and re-encoded as PNG; manufacturer logos removed (button symbols and letters kept); compiled to Sightline's native .slmodel format with a part table

authored_parts.btn_guide: plain btn_guide replacing the original logo-shaped part

authored_parts_note: These parts are the project owner's own replacement geometry (manufacturer logos removed); everything else in the mesh and every texture is the third party's CC-BY-4.0 work as changed above.
debranding: btn_guide: the embossed manufacturer logo (an 836-face shell) and its dome replaced by an owner-authored plain dome of the same footprint, textured with the plain disc colour the original used (extras.sl_authored_part on the node).
frame: GjoypadZ: +x = player's right, +y = up toward the watch camera, -z = the top edge; N64 body 788 x 253 x 836; fitted to width 788
parts_note: package node label (extras.sl_part) -> canonical physical part (tools/asset/gltf_import.py PARTS); physical controls only, never actions
source_oracle_note: sha1 of the owner's staged package files as received (2026-09-19); the .bin and textures are committed verbatim, the .gltf's extras were rewritten
